105 ./verification/testing/gates/SKILL.md
## 1. Regressions

Every batch checks, formats and lints the workspace on the tree it lands, with warnings
denied, as [`toolchain`](../../../rust/toolchain/SKILL.md) describes, and tests what its
change can affect: its module and the modules that depend on it, as `modules.json` records
them, each by its tests' module paths.

Every build of those gates runs in the raw bindings' campaign mode, as
[`bindgen`](../../../rust/bindgen/SKILL.md)'s Build modes section describes, so that each fails when the
committed bindings do not match their input. A batch that changed the raw bindings, or a
landing that changes `c/`, also packages the safe crate, built alone in bundled mode from
the C it packages, with no build variant selected. Until the out-of-tree wrappers are
published, each crate the package depends on is patched to its local source, so that the
package builds alone.

The tests run against the matching variant, or a private replacement, and each event runs
them to its own depth:

- a batch: the tests above, plain and under ASan/UBSan, and its own tests under each other
  sanitizer its items call for, such as TSan where it asserts `Send` or `Sync` or adds a
  threaded callback, or MSan where C leaves memory it hands over partly unwritten;
- a wave's end: the workspace's tests, and the Miri gate below;
- a module's end, its switch in a port: every test under every available sanitizer,
  and BSan as below; and
- a ship point: every gate over the whole workspace under every available sanitizer, with
  the coverage measurement.
<!-- TODO: a wave's end and a module's end are run by the wave's last review batch and the
module pass, so a campaign without review runs neither: they need an owner there. -->

BSan, when available, is run for every batch and at module end:

- For a batch, it runs only on the individual tests or reproducers the batch expects to
  trigger it, each by exact name and alone; never on a whole test binary, a suite or the
  workspace.
- At module end, it runs as a gate over everything the module landed: the
  whole workspace, one invocation per test binary, as many side by side as
  [`concurrency`](../../../operations/concurrency/SKILL.md) describes, each under a `timeout`.

A batch runs the tests it wrote under Miri. Miri is also run after every wave, as a gate
over the whole workspace: one Miri run on the pinned nightly per test binary, the library's
and each integration suite's, as many side by side as
[`concurrency`](../../../operations/concurrency/SKILL.md) describes, each skipping the
compile-fail tests. The gate passes only
with no Miri error: a test that stops at the foreign boundary without the attribute gets
it, and any other Miri error is a UB candidate of the item it touches.

`end-gates`, beside this skill and documented by its `--help`, runs a wave's and a
module's end gates so, over a snapshot of the tree, so that work goes on in the tree while
they run: the workspace under each variant, Miri and BSan per test binary, and the BSan
tests known never to finish skipped by name, each skip checked against its binary's test
list before anything runs.

Each gate run starts in the background and is waited on to exit; its output is neither
polled nor read while it runs. BSan reports false positives at the foreign boundary, so
only a true positive, a report that reproduces through the Rust side as a single test or
standalone reproducer, becomes a UB finding.

Every translation and review batch measures the consumer-facing API of its items against
the tip it rebased onto, each change classified as the dashboard's API stability columns
name them. An item's API is fixed by its first landing: a later landing
that changes or removes it, a port, a later stage, a rebind or a review fix alike, breaks
its consumers, and is kept only with its reason recorded in the batch's notes, such as a
soundness fix; the measure does not fail the gate. A module's integration measures every
item of the module against the module's base, and a ship point the whole crate against the
previous ship point.

When C changed, the configured C build and baseline run. A wrap-only batch with no C
change does not need the full C baseline.

A batch validates its own change on its own base first. Its rebase onto the integration
branch, under the landing lock that [`versioning`](../../../operations/versioning/SKILL.md)'s Landing section
describes, then combines that change with the work landed since: the gates run again are
those that could catch a regression the combination introduces, judged from what the
batch's change and the rebased-in changes touch and how they could interact. A gate that
neither side's changes could affect keeps the result it had, and a rebase that conflicts
makes the resolved tree new work of the batch's own.

A `port` batch changes no C: its gates are those above, run against the variants with its
module's export feature off, so that the ported Rust is tested beside the C it replaces.
It also checks and lints the safe crate with that feature on, which compiles the module's
gateway without linking it, and each export is checked at compile time against the raw
binding of the C declaration it replaces, so that a signature that drifts from C's fails
to build.

A module's switch removes its translation unit, and the C tests tied to it that reach
its internals, from `c/`, rebuilds the variants from the C that remains and deletes the
module's export feature, as
[`porting-workflow`](../../../workflows/porting-workflow/SKILL.md)'s Builds section
describes. Its gates are a module's end's, in campaign mode over the rebuilt variants, and
the target's remaining C tests, which link the remaining C and the safe crate's Rust static
library, so that the C reaches the ported module through its exports: the module's tied C
tests that use only its public API among them, as the porting workflow's Tests follow
their modules section describes. Before a tied C test leaves, the cases none of the
module's `unit_pub` tests carries over are listed, as [`testing`](../SKILL.md)'s C tests
carried over section describes.

opt.c: switch from C to Rust (modules/git2/src/cli/opt.c/integration/run-1)

src/cli/opt.c is the second module to switch, and the first of the git2
link unit, the CLI: its export feature, ffi-export-src-cli-opt-c, is
deleted, so that opt.rs's gateway, with its six unit_priv tests, compiles
from now on, and the fork's main drops the TU (c/ at f57e1a616,
`integrate src/cli/opt.c`). The CLI's remaining C, main.c, the cmd_*.c
commands, common.c and opt_usage.c, reaches cli_opt_parser_init,
cli_opt_parser_next, cli_opt_parse, cli_opt_foreach and
cli_opt_status_fprint through the exports, in the crate's static library
the CLI already links (LIBGIT2_RUST_LIBRARY). opt.h stays, for common.h.

The module's equivalence tests, which need the C, are retired
(tests/equiv/src/cli/opt.rs, and tests/equiv/src/cli.rs with it). Two of
them read only opt.h's constants through the raw bindings and ran no C,
and no unit test kept what they established, the usage and parse flags'
bits being C's: they move to tests/unit_pub/src/cli/opt.rs. The raw
bindings of the five exported functions stay and reach the exports, and
the module has no unexported function bound, so no allowlist entry goes;
the types stay for the layouts the CLI's C builds and reads.

The gateway's tests ran under TSan for the first time, once they compiled
without the feature: the_status_message_describes_a_failed_parse read the
export's errno after closing its memory stream, whose fclose and free
TSan's interceptors leave EBADF behind, and now reads it right after the
call.

commit f68ea8660adf7dcc618e2ff25cea15eeb2c0581a
Author: Marius Momeu <marius.momeu@berkeley.edu>
Date:   Sat Nov 14 01:04:12 2026 +0000

    opt.c: switch from C to Rust (modules/git2/src/cli/opt.c/integration/run-1)
    
    src/cli/opt.c is the second module to switch, and the first of the git2
    link unit, the CLI: its export feature, ffi-export-src-cli-opt-c, is
    deleted, so that opt.rs's gateway, with its six unit_priv tests, compiles
    from now on, and the fork's main drops the TU (c/ at f57e1a616,
    `integrate src/cli/opt.c`). The CLI's remaining C, main.c, the cmd_*.c
    commands, common.c and opt_usage.c, reaches cli_opt_parser_init,
    cli_opt_parser_next, cli_opt_parse, cli_opt_foreach and
    cli_opt_status_fprint through the exports, in the crate's static library
    the CLI already links (LIBGIT2_RUST_LIBRARY). opt.h stays, for common.h.
    
    The module's equivalence tests, which need the C, are retired
    (tests/equiv/src/cli/opt.rs, and tests/equiv/src/cli.rs with it). Two of
    them read only opt.h's constants through the raw bindings and ran no C,
    and no unit test kept what they established, the usage and parse flags'
    bits being C's: they move to tests/unit_pub/src/cli/opt.rs. The raw
    bindings of the five exported functions stay and reach the exports, and
    the module has no unexported function bound, so no allowlist entry goes;
    the types stay for the layouts the CLI's C builds and reads.
    
    The gateway's tests ran under TSan for the first time, once they compiled
    without the feature: the_status_message_describes_a_failed_parse read the
    export's errno after closing its memory stream, whose fclose and free
    TSan's interceptors leave EBADF behind, and now reads it right after the
    call.
    
    Co-Authored-By: crustify <crustify@berkeley.edu>

## 4. Extending

The bindings grow with the batches: a batch whose items need a raw binding the bindings
lack extends its own link unit's input, and nothing else:

1. its link unit's `allowlist.txt` gains only the FFI items its items need, and
   `wrapper.h` an internal header only when one of them is declared there;
2. a shim is added to `shims.h` and `shims.c` only for a macro whose expansion depends on
   the build's configuration, as `crustify_<NAME>`, as
   [`binding-symbols`](../binding/symbols/SKILL.md)'s Macros section describes;
3. the bindings are regenerated, in campaign mode with `CRUSTIFY_BINDINGS_UPDATE` set; and
4. the safe crate is built and tested against them.

Where its link unit's headers name a type another link unit owns, the batch also extends
what the re-export needs, and only that: the type joins its own link unit's `external.txt`,
the owning link unit's `allowlist.txt` too while its bindings lack the type, and the link
unit's module in `src/sys.rs` re-exports it from the owner's, under its C name.

An allowlist or `wrapper.h` change alone leaves the C library as it is, so it reuses a
prebuilt variant; a shim compiles with the crate, as [Build modes](#3-build-modes) describes.

## 5. Landing

#!/bin/bash
# Build a generation of the target's variants from the C that remains (crustify's setup
# skill, Builds; porting-workflow, Builds): run after a module's switch removes C, and
# whenever the shared variants are rebuilt.
#
#   build-variants.sh <generation dir> [<variant>...]
#
# A generation is a directory beside crustify/builds, as crustify/builds.gen<n>, which a
# checkout's crustify/builds links to once it is built: it holds `c`, a detached worktree
# of this checkout's `c/` repository at the commit `c/` has checked out, which `c/` must
# hold without changes, and one build dir per variant of crustify/artifacts/build.json
# (every one by default), named as its `dir` names it. Each variant's `configure` and
# `build` commands run from its dir, physically resolved, so that the relative paths they
# take (the generation's `../c`, the side campaigns' installs four levels up) resolve as
# for the shared builds, with CRUSTIFY_ROOT set to this checkout, whose scripts the
# commands run and whose Rust the C consumers link. The variants build side by side, each
# logging to <dir>/crustify/build.log; the exit status is 1 when any fails, naming it.
# An existing generation is not rebuilt: a variant whose dir exists is refused.
set -euo pipefail
usage='usage: build-variants.sh <generation dir> [<variant>...]'
gen=${1:?$usage}
shift
root=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
spec=$root/crustify/artifacts/build.json
mapfile -t all < <(python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; print("\n".join(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["variants"]))' "$spec")
variants=("$@")
[ ${#variants[@]} -gt 0 ] || variants=("${all[@]}")
for v in "${variants[@]}"; do
  printf '%s\n' "${all[@]}" | grep -qx -- "$v" || { echo "build-variants.sh: no variant $v in $spec" >&2; exit 2; }
done

mkdir -p "$gen"
gen=$(cd -P "$gen" && pwd)
commit=$(git -C "$root/c" rev-parse HEAD)
if [ ! -e "$gen/c" ]; then
  [ -z "$(git -C "$root/c" status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" ] || {
    echo "build-variants.sh: $root/c has changes: a generation is built from a commit" >&2
    exit 1
  }
  git -C "$root/c" worktree add --detach "$gen/c" "$commit" >/dev/null
fi
held=$(git -C "$gen/c" rev-parse HEAD)
[ "$held" = "$commit" ] || {
  echo "build-variants.sh: $gen/c holds $held, not $root/c's $commit" >&2
  exit 1
}

field() { python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["variants"][sys.argv[2]][sys.argv[3]])' "$spec" "$1" "$2"; }

pids=() names=()
for v in "${variants[@]}"; do
  dir=$gen/$(basename "$(field "$v" dir)")
  [ ! -e "$dir" ] || { echo "build-variants.sh: $dir exists: a generation is built once" >&2; exit 1; }
  mkdir -p "$dir/crustify"
  configure=$(field "$v" configure)
  build=$(field "$v" build)
  (
    cd -P "$dir"
    export CRUSTIFY_ROOT=$root
    {
      echo "+ $configure"
      eval "$configure"
      echo "+ $build"
      eval "$build"
    } >"$dir/crustify/build.log" 2>&1
  ) &
  pids+=($!) names+=("$v")
done
failed=()
for i in "${!pids[@]}"; do
  wait "${pids[$i]}" || failed+=("${names[$i]}")
done
if [ ${#failed[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "build-variants.sh: ${failed[*]} failed: see each <dir>/crustify/build.log under $gen" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "build-variants.sh: $gen holds ${variants[*]}, from c/ at $commit"
#!/bin/bash

# baseline (crustify's testing-gates skill, Regressions: a module's switch; setup, Baseline).
#
#   c-tests.sh <variant dir> <out dir> [jobs]

# crate's Rust static library; its name is the variant whose record of
# crustify/artifacts/c-baseline.json the run is compared with. Nothing is written into it:
# every output goes under <out dir>.
#
# 1. build.json's `test` command, `ctest --output-on-failure -R '^(offline|util)$'`, over a
#    copy of the variant's CTestTestfile.cmake tree, so that ctest's own records stay out of
#    the variant, beside the suites of step 2: <out dir>/ctest.log, its exit status in
#    <out dir>/ctest.rc.
# 2. Every offline libgit2_tests suite and every util_tests suite alone, <jobs> side by side
#    (default 8), each under a 30-minute timeout, as the baseline ran them: TAP output in
#    <out dir>/suites/<binary>/<suite>.{tap,err,rc}. `online::*` suites need the network and
#    are left out, as the `offline` ctest target leaves them.
# 3. The tally, <out dir>/tally.json (cases passed, failed and skipped, and every suite that
#    failed a case or exited non-zero, with the sanitizer reports it printed), compared with
#    the baseline's record: the exit status is 0 when the case counts and the non-zero suites
#    (binary, suite, exit status) match it, and 1 otherwise, naming each difference. ctest's
#    status is reported beside it; under TSan the baseline's own races fail `offline`.

usage='usage: c-tests.sh <variant dir> <out dir> [jobs]'
d=$(cd -P "${1:?$usage}" && pwd) || exit 2
out=${2:?$usage}
jobs=${3:-8}
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
variant=$(basename "$d")
[ -x "$d/libgit2_tests" ] && [ -x "$d/util_tests" ] || { echo "c-tests.sh: $d has no C tests built" >&2; exit 2; }
mkdir -p "$out"
out=$(cd -P "$out" && pwd)
export LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=${LLVM_PROFILE_FILE:-/dev/null}

# 1. ctest, over a copy of the test files: they name the executables by absolute path.
rm -rf "$out/ctest"
mkdir -p "$out/ctest"
(cd "$d" && find . -name CTestTestfile.cmake -not -path './crustify/*' -exec cp --parents {} "$out/ctest" \;)

(
  ctest --test-dir "$out/ctest" --output-on-failure -R '^(offline|util)$' >"$out/ctest.log" 2>&1
  echo $? >"$out/ctest.rc"
) &

  mkdir -p "$out/suites/$b"

    D="$d" O="$out" B="$b" xargs -P "$jobs" -I{} bash -c \

#!/bin/bash
# Build a generation of the target's variants from the C that remains (crustify's setup
# skill, Builds; porting-workflow, Builds): run after a module's switch removes C, and
# whenever the shared variants are rebuilt.
#
#   build-variants.sh <generation dir> [<variant>...]
#
# A generation is a directory beside crustify/builds, as crustify/builds.gen<n>, which a
# checkout's crustify/builds links to once it is built: it holds `c`, a detached worktree
# of this checkout's `c/` repository at the commit `c/` has checked out, which `c/` must
# hold without changes, and one build dir per variant of crustify/artifacts/build.json
# (every one by default), named as its `dir` names it. Each variant's `configure` and
# `build` commands run from its dir, physically resolved, so that the relative paths they
# take (the generation's `../c`, the side campaigns' installs four levels up) resolve as
# for the shared builds, with CRUSTIFY_ROOT set to this checkout, whose scripts the
# commands run and whose Rust the C consumers link. The variants build side by side, each
# logging to <dir>/crustify/build.log; the exit status is 1 when any fails, naming it.
# An existing generation is not rebuilt: a variant whose dir exists is refused.
set -euo pipefail
usage='usage: build-variants.sh <generation dir> [<variant>...]'
gen=${1:?$usage}
shift
root=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
spec=$root/crustify/artifacts/build.json
mapfile -t all < <(python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; print("\n".join(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["variants"]))' "$spec")
variants=("$@")
[ ${#variants[@]} -gt 0 ] || variants=("${all[@]}")
for v in "${variants[@]}"; do
  printf '%s\n' "${all[@]}" | grep -qx -- "$v" || { echo "build-variants.sh: no variant $v in $spec" >&2; exit 2; }
done

mkdir -p "$gen"
gen=$(cd -P "$gen" && pwd)
commit=$(git -C "$root/c" rev-parse HEAD)
if [ ! -e "$gen/c" ]; then
  [ -z "$(git -C "$root/c" status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" ] || {
    echo "build-variants.sh: $root/c has changes: a generation is built from a commit" >&2
    exit 1
  }
  git -C "$root/c" worktree add --detach "$gen/c" "$commit" >/dev/null
fi
held=$(git -C "$gen/c" rev-parse HEAD)
[ "$held" = "$commit" ] || {
  echo "build-variants.sh: $gen/c holds $held, not $root/c's $commit" >&2
  exit 1
}

field() { python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["variants"][sys.argv[2]][sys.argv[3]])' "$spec" "$1" "$2"; }

pids=() names=()
for v in "${variants[@]}"; do
  dir=$gen/$(basename "$(field "$v" dir)")
  [ ! -e "$dir" ] || { echo "build-variants.sh: $dir exists: a generation is built once" >&2; exit 1; }
  mkdir -p "$dir/crustify"
  configure=$(field "$v" configure)
  build=$(field "$v" build)
  (
    cd -P "$dir"
    export CRUSTIFY_ROOT=$root
    {
      echo "+ $configure"
      eval "$configure"
      echo "+ $build"
      eval "$build"
    } >"$dir/crustify/build.log" 2>&1
  ) &
  pids+=($!) names+=("$v")
done
failed=()
for i in "${!pids[@]}"; do
  wait "${pids[$i]}" || failed+=("${names[$i]}")
done
if [ ${#failed[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "build-variants.sh: ${failed[*]} failed: see each <dir>/crustify/build.log under $gen" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "build-variants.sh: $gen holds ${variants[*]}, from c/ at $commit"

#!/bin/bash
# Run cargo against one crustify prebuild of libgit2, instrumenting Rust to match.
#
#   crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh <variant> <cargo subcommand> [args...]
#
# <variant> is a `variants` key of crustify/artifacts/build.json: plain, coverage, asan-ubsan,
# tsan or bsan. Each variant uses its own target dir under target/.
# The safe crate's build script, in campaign mode, links the variant's static archive (its
# `static` in build.json) into each test binary, so the C runs under the instrumentation the
# Rust is built with here, one runtime serving both. Set CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR to a private build
# of the variant, which carries the same archive, to link it instead of the shared one.
set -euo pipefail
variant=${1:?usage: cargo-variant.sh <variant> <cargo subcommand> [args...]}
shift
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=$variant
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-$here/target/$variant}
# pcre2-sys links the variant's side-campaign PCRE2, the one libgit2's C links, rather than
# building its vendored copy, which would shadow it in every test binary. The side campaigns'
# clones sit where the variant's build found their installs, beside the repository whose
# crustify/builds holds it (build.json's configure takes them from `$PWD/../../../..` in
# crustify/builds/<variant>): resolved physically through crustify/builds, which a worktree or
# a gate snapshot links to that repository's, so that every checkout finds the same ones.
side=$(realpath -m "$here/crustify/builds/$variant/../../../..")
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$side/pcre2-bindings/crustify/builds/$variant/install/lib/pkgconfig${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:+:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH}"
cd "$here"
# The nightly the workspace pins, for the sanitizers that need it.
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' Cargo.toml)
# Cargo's own flags must come before a `--`, which hands the rest to the test binaries.
pre=() post=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ ${#post[@]} -gt 0 ] || [ "$arg" = -- ]; then post+=("$arg"); else pre+=("$arg"); fi
done
case $variant in
  plain)
    exec cargo "$@" ;;
  coverage)
    # Source-based coverage on the pinned nightly, against the variant's clang-instrumented C,
    # which each test binary links statically, so that rustc's profiler runtime counts both;

content.content:
1:#!/bin/bash
2:# Build the safe crate's Rust static library for a variant's own C to link (crustify's
3:# porting-workflow skill, Builds): once a module has switched from C, the remaining C, its
4:# library, CLI and tests, reaches the module through the crate's exports, and its CMake
5:# build links this library (`LIBGIT2_RUST_LIBRARY`).
6:#
7:#   rust-staticlib.sh <variant> <archive>
8:#
9:# Run from the variant's build dir, configured and not yet built, as the first step of its
10:# `build` command in crustify/artifacts/build.json; <archive> is the library written,
11:# relative to the build dir, as its configure's `-DLIBGIT2_RUST_LIBRARY` names it. The crate
12:# is the one of the checkout this script belongs to, built as a `staticlib` on the dev
13:# profile, the campaign's tests' own, in campaign mode against this build dir
14:# (`CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR`) with `CRUSTIFY_STATICLIB` set, so that it reads the build's headers
15:# and configuration and links none of its C, and with the `bindgen` feature, so that the
16:# committed bindings are checked against them. Its Rust is instrumented as
17:# crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh instruments <variant>'s, so that one runtime serves the C
18:# and the Rust of every C consumer. Cargo's target dir is the build's own, `crustify/cargo`;
19:# the archive is replaced atomically, so that a link never reads a partial one.
35:export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$build/crustify/cargo
40:    out=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/debug

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A smart-HTTP Git remote on localhost, for the C that drives libgit2's HTTP client.

    http-remote.py <root> <port file> [--auth USER:PASS] [--log FILE]

Serves the repositories under <root> through `git http-backend`, upload-pack and
receive-pack both, over HTTP/1.1 with persistent connections, so that libgit2's HTTP
client (src/libgit2/transports/httpclient.c over httpparser.c and llhttp) reads several
responses on one connection. It listens on 127.0.0.1 at a port the system picks, written to
<port file> once it accepts connections, and runs until killed.

The first component of a request's path picks how the response's body is framed, the rest
naming the repository under <root>, so that one remote serves every framing llhttp parses:

- `/length/<repo>`: a `Content-Length` body;
- `/chunked/<repo>`: `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, in chunks of 1, 7, 4096 and 65536 bytes
  in turn, so that a chunk's size line, its data and its end fall across reads;
- `/chunked-ext/<repo>`: chunked as above, every size line carrying chunk extensions
  (`;a=b;flag;q="x y"`), which llhttp's chunk-extension callbacks are called for;
- `/close/<repo>`: no length and no chunking, the body ending with the connection
  (`Connection: close`).

With `--auth`, every request without that user's Basic credentials is answered 401 with a
`WWW-Authenticate: Basic` challenge, a body and the connection kept, before the backend
runs. A path that names no repository is the backend's 404. Requests are logged to
`--log`, one line each, method, path and status, for the caller to compare.

Crustify's campaign check of a module whose exports libgit2's HTTP client reaches, at its
switch from C (crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure): run it with `python3 -I`.
"""

import base64
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

CHUNKS = (1, 7, 4096, 65536)
FRAMINGS = ("length", "chunked", "chunked-ext", "close")


def main(argv):

#!/bin/bash
# Drive libgit2's HTTP client through a variant's own C, over a smart-HTTP remote on localhost
# (crustify's testing-gates skill, Regressions: a module's switch, for a module whose exports
# the HTTP client reaches, which no offline C test does; crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure).
#
#   http-gate.sh <variant dir> <out dir>
#
# <variant dir> is a built variant, crustify/builds.gen<n>/<variant>, with its `git2` and
# `libgit2_tests`; nothing is written into it. Two remotes are started from
# crustify/scripts/http-remote.py over scratch repositories under <out dir>/remotes, one open
# and one asking for Basic credentials (foo:bar), each serving every framing it offers
# (Content-Length, chunked, chunked with extensions, close-delimited):
#
# 1. the variant's `git2 clone` of testrepo.git (c/tests/resources) and of a 100-commit
#    shallow history of the generation's c/ at a fixed commit, through each framing, and
#    clones that fail: a missing repository (404) and the guarded remote without credentials
#    (401); each clone's exit status, refs, HEAD, checked-out tree and `git fsck` outcome;
# 2. the variant's `libgit2_tests -sonline::push -sonline::clone::credentials`, libgit2's own
#    C tests of a push and a clone over GITTEST_REMOTE_URL, against the guarded remote with
#    foo:bar, through each framing: its TAP tally.
#
# <out dir>/results.txt is one line per case, free of times, ports and paths, so that two
# generations' results compare with `diff`; every process's output is kept beside it, and each
# line counts the sanitizer reports that process printed (`reports=`). The exit status is 0
# when every clone that should succeed did and every suite passed, 1 otherwise.
set -uo pipefail
usage='usage: http-gate.sh <variant dir> <out dir>'
d=$(cd -P "${1:?$usage}" && pwd) || exit 2
out=${2:?$usage}
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
c=$(cd -P "$d/../c" && pwd) || { echo "http-gate.sh: no generation c/ beside $d" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -x "$d/git2" ] && [ -x "$d/libgit2_tests" ] || { echo "http-gate.sh: $d has no git2 or libgit2_tests" >&2; exit 2; }
rm -rf "$out"
mkdir -p "$out"
out=$(cd -P "$out" && pwd)
export LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=${LLVM_PROFILE_FILE:-/dev/null}
export GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='2026-01-01T00:00:00Z' GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='2026-01-01T00:00:00Z'
# The shallow history's tip: the campaign's source revision, which every generation's c/ holds.
big_tip=0551dfd4a
framings=(length chunked chunked-ext close)
status=0
results=$out/results.txt
: >"$results"
reports() { grep -cE 'WARNING: ThreadSanitizer|ERROR: AddressSanitizer|ERROR: LeakSanitizer|runtime error:' "$@" 2>/dev/null | awk -F: '{s+=$NF} END {print s+0}'; }

# The remotes' repositories.
r=$out/remotes
mkdir -p "$r/open" "$r/guarded"
git clone -q --bare "$c/tests/resources/testrepo.git" "$r/open/testrepo.git"
git init -q --bare "$r/open/big.git"
git -C "$r/open/big.git" -c protocol.file.allow=always fetch -q --depth=100 "file://$c" \
  "$(git -C "$c" rev-parse "$big_tip")":refs/heads/main
git -C "$r/open/big.git" symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main
git -C "$r/open/big.git" repack -q -a -d
for f in "${framings[@]}"; do git init -q --bare "$r/guarded/push-$f.git"; done
git clone -q --bare "$c/tests/resources/testrepo.git" "$r/guarded/testrepo.git"

pids=()
trap 'kill "${pids[@]}" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
python3 -I "$here/http-remote.py" "$r/open" "$out/open.port" --log "$out/open.log" &
pids+=($!)
python3 -I "$here/http-remote.py" "$r/guarded" "$out/guarded.port" --auth foo:bar --log "$out/guarded.log" &
pids+=($!)
for _ in $(seq 100); do [ -s "$out/open.port" ] && [ -s "$out/guarded.port" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
open=http://127.0.0.1:$(cat "$out/open.port")
guarded=http://127.0.0.1:$(cat "$out/guarded.port")

# 1. The CLI's clones. <expect> is ok or fail.
clone() {
  local name=$1 url=$2 expect=$3 dir=$out/clones/$1
  mkdir -p "$out/clones"
  (cd "$out/clones" && timeout 600 "$d/git2" clone "$url" "$dir" >"$dir.out" 2>"$dir.err" </dev/null)
  local rc=$? line="clone $name rc=$rc"
  if [ $rc -eq 0 ] && [ -d "$dir/.git" ]; then
    local refs head tree fsck
    refs=$(git -C "$dir" for-each-ref --format='%(objectname) %(refname)' | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
    head=$(git -C "$dir" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null)
    tree=$(git -C "$dir" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
    git -C "$dir" fsck --strict --no-progress >"$dir.fsck" 2>&1 && fsck=ok || fsck=failed
    line+=" refs=$refs head=$head status=$tree fsck=$fsck"
  else
    line+=" error=\"$(grep -v '^\s*$' "$dir.err" | grep -vE 'Sanitizer|^ +#|^SUMMARY|^==' | tail -1)\""
  fi
  line+=" reports=$(reports "$dir.err")"
  echo "$line" >>"$results"
  case $expect in
    ok) [ $rc -eq 0 ] && [[ $line == *fsck=ok* ]] || status=1 ;;
    fail) [ $rc -ne 0 ] || status=1 ;;
  esac

The gates of testing-gates' Regressions section, run exactly so:

1. The tree's commit (`--rev`, HEAD by default), or its working tree with
   `--working-tree`, is copied to a snapshot, `<tree>/crustify/tmp/gates-<label>`, so that
   work goes on in the tree while the gates run. Each submodule, and each `--link` path
   (such as the variants' builds dir), is symlinked from the tree into it, and the snapshot
   is made a git repository, since a test may discover the repository it runs in.
2. Each skip of `--skip-file` is checked against its test binary's `--list` before any
   stage runs: a skip that names no test, or that would also skip another, since libtest
   skips by substring, fails the run.
3. The stages run in the order given:
   - a variant (`plain` and each sanitizer but `bsan`): the workspace's tests,
     `<runner> <variant> test --workspace --no-fail-fast`, with that stage's skips;
   - `miri`: the package's test binaries built once on the pinned nightly, then one
     `cargo miri test` per test binary, side by side, each skipping `compile_fail`;
   - `bsan`: the test binaries built once, then one invocation per test binary, side by
     side, each under `--timeout`, with that stage's skips.
4. Each run writes `<logs>/<stage>[-<binary>].log`; `<logs>/summary.json` and
   `summary.txt` record each run's command, exit status, duration, test-result lines and
   failed tests. A run that exceeds its timeout reports `timed_out`.

being `lib` or an integration test's name; `#` starts a comment. A variant stage's skips
apply to every binary of the workspace.

The job count is the environment's: `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` for builds, `RUST_TEST_THREADS` for
each binary's tests, as concurrency describes. The exit status is 0 when every run
passed, 1 when any failed, and 2 when the run could not start.

no export, the getters, the name functions, llhttp_settings_init,
llhttp_reset, llhttp_set_error_reason and the ten lenient setters, which
only api.c's equivalence tests called, go with their allowlist entries.

### `libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c` wave 194 batch 7: module pass

The module pass, over api.c's whole module across its batches (`api.rs` and its `equiv`,
`ub_safe` and `unit_pub` files), for every objective with `fix`, and the wave's and the
module's end gates. `llhttp.rs`'s twelve units bound ahead were read, not reported on. It
files two findings, `+equiv` and `+misc`, both fixed.

- **equiv**: `llhttp_execute`'s export read a run of 0 bytes as `&[]`, whose address is
  `0x1`. A run of 0 bytes that ends a span the previous run left open, refused by the span's
  callback, so left `error_pos` at `0x1`, where api.c's `llhttp__internal_execute(parser,
  data, data + len)` leaves it at `data`. `git_http_parser_execute` subtracts `data` from it.
  libgit2's C calls `llhttp_finish` for an empty run, so it does not reach this. A reproducer
  runs the export beside api.c's body, with the exports linked in place of `api.c.o`, and
  exits 101. The export now reads any non-NULL `data` as its `len` bytes, an empty run
  included. The regression test is the gateway's `unit_priv`
  `llhttp_execute_keeps_an_empty_runs_error_pos_at_data`.
- **misc**: `equiv` is one binary for every module, and `llhttp.c`'s equivalence tests,
  which stay, also read their parsers through api.c's getters, its name functions and
  `llhttp_settings_init`. None of those has an export, so with `api.c.o` out of the archive
  `equiv` did not link even with api.c's own file retired (`rust-lld`: 23 undefined
  symbols, 10 of them from `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs`). Batches 4 and 6 had left
  `equiv` out of their link checks as a whole. The nine tests that compare `llhttp.rs`'s
  accessors and maps with api.c's functions moved, unchanged, into an inline `getters` module
  of `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/api.rs`. So retiring that one file, with its `mod api;`, is
  api.c's whole equivalence retirement at the switch.

The retirement removes 21 `equiv` tests. The report maps each to the `unit_pub` tests that
keep what it established. Five new `unit_pub` tests keep what no unit test kept: what a
response read in pieces leaves the getters, an unnamed status, a request's method and a
`CONNECT`'s upgrade, an error located in sub-slices, a callback's own error read as unnamed,
and the type a setter sets deciding the next parse. A new gateway test,
`each_dispatcher_export_calls_its_own_slot`, checks that each of the 23 exports `llhttp.c`
calls by name reaches its own slot, which only the retiring `equiv` test did for all of them.
What no test keeps, and none needs once the C is gone: that each operation leaves the private
parser state byte for byte as C's did from six states, and that the lenient setters read any
nonzero `int` as true.

What held. The unsafe regions' justifications hold on every path: the table read, the slot
calls, the type byte, `reinit_keeping_context` and `stderr`, and `Settings`' `CZeroable`,
`Send` and `Sync`. Batch 6's corrected `set_settings_ptr`, `set_data` and `parser_mut`
contracts stand. The 31 exports are every api.c symbol the remaining C references:
`httpparser.c` (`llhttp_execute`, `llhttp_finish`, `llhttp_get_error_pos`,
`llhttp_resume_after_upgrade`), `httpparser.h`'s macros (`llhttp_init`, `llhttp_pause`,
`llhttp_resume`, `llhttp_get_error_reason`) and `llhttp.c`'s 23 dispatchers. No C test,
`http.c` or other C file calls another. The exports keep what that C relies on: the error
position inside the run, the reason a `'static` C string, `llhttp_pause` safe from inside
`on_headers_complete`, and no unwind into C. `libgit2.so` keeps their symbols local
(`--exclude-libs`, `utf8.c`'s switch). No offline C test drives the HTTP client:
`tests/libgit2/core/features.c` only names the parser. So after the switch the exports are
checked by the gateway's eight `unit_priv` tests, which then always compile, by the safe API's
`unit_pub` and `ub_safe` tests, and by libgit2's `online` suites (`online::clone`,
`online::fetch`, `online::push` over HTTP), which the C baseline disables and need the network.

Gates, at 24 jobs, without BSan (the settings' `sanitizers` answer). On the tip `9124cc5a6`
(`end-gates` snapshot): plain passes the whole workspace (`lib` 854 and 1 ignored, `equiv`
553, `ub_safe` 785, `ub_unsafe` 137, `unit_pub` 156, `hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 92 and
387). ASan+UBSan and TSan pass it but for the known `compile_fail` snapshot and `CommitBuilder`
doctest. Miri passes every binary (`lib` 406, `equiv` 38, `ub_safe` 201, `unit_pub` 85,
`ub_unsafe` 19 passed, the rest marked). On this tree, `fmt` and `clippy --workspace
--all-targets` pass with warnings denied with the export feature off and on. On `b5eda0b43`'s tree (`end-gates`), plain passes the whole
workspace (`lib` 854 and 1 ignored, `equiv` 553, `unit_pub` 161, the rest as on the tip), and
ASan+UBSan and TSan pass it but for the known failures. Miri the changed binaries: `unit_pub` 85 and `equiv` 38 passed, the rest marked, and with
the feature on the gateway's 12, `each_dispatcher_export_calls_its_own_slot` among them. Each
new test marked `calls C` was run alone under Miri and stops at `llhttp__internal_init`.
With the exports linked in place of `api.c.o` (`crustify/tmp/linkcheck/<variant>`, archive
copies of 211 objects named by `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR`), and `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/api.rs`
retired in a scratch tree as the switch will retire it, the whole workspace passes on plain
(`lib` 861 and 1 ignored, `equiv` 532, `ub_safe` 785, `ub_unsafe` 137, `unit_pub` 161,
`hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 92 and 387). ASan+UBSan and TSan pass it but for the known
failures. `nm` shows the 31 exports defined and no other api.c symbol.

Coverage: `run.sh` on a `git archive` of the tip and on this tree, read with `report.py` from
each scratch tree's `src/libgit2`, the unit column merging `lib` and `unit_pub`. The totals
move from `47.26`% / `98.69`% to `47.24`% / `98.69`%; the C deltas but unit's are run-to-run
noise, since those suites run the same tests. Worklist: `api.rs` 187 of 187 lines, 39 of 39
functions, 226 of 227 regions; the gateway compiles out with the feature off. The new unit
tests take `llhttp.rs` from 289 to 291 of its 310 lines under the unit column. `api.c` keeps
267 of its 283 lines and 54 of 55 functions under `equiv`, `llhttp__debug` the one left. The
safety audit scan (ffimap `9aa2ef1`, flags as batch 6's, the export feature on) differs from
the tip's only in test counters (`code.tests.loc.total` `+243`, which the Overview takes).
`ffimap api` against the tip (nightly `2026-10-08`, ffibox's private rustdoc JSON): the 65
anchored keys are `kept`, the two private macro ports `missing`, and every unattributed module
`kept`. No raw binding or C changed, so the packaging gate does not apply. The `+unit` cell
counts the five `unit_pub` tests; the gateway's two compile out with the feature off.
Usage cells are the assistant's.

  of `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/api.rs`. So retiring that one file, with its `mod api;`, is
  api.c's whole equivalence retirement at the switch.

The retirement removes 21 `equiv` tests. The report maps each to the `unit_pub` tests that
keep what it established. Five new `unit_pub` tests keep what no unit test kept: what a
response read in pieces leaves the getters, an unnamed status, a request's method and a
`CONNECT`'s upgrade, an error located in sub-slices, a callback's own error read as unnamed,
and the type a setter sets deciding the next parse. A new gateway test,
`each_dispatcher_export_calls_its_own_slot`, checks that each of the 23 exports `llhttp.c`
calls by name reaches its own slot, which only the retiring `equiv` test did for all of them.
What no test keeps, and none needs once the C is gone: that each operation leaves the private
parser state byte for byte as C's did from six states, and that the lenient setters read any
nonzero `int` as true.

What held. The unsafe regions' justifications hold on every path: the table read, the slot
calls, the type byte, `reinit_keeping_context` and `stderr`, and `Settings`' `CZeroable`,
`Send` and `Sync`. Batch 6's corrected `set_settings_ptr`, `set_data` and `parser_mut`
contracts stand. The 31 exports are every api.c symbol the remaining C references:
`httpparser.c` (`llhttp_execute`, `llhttp_finish`, `llhttp_get_error_pos`,
`llhttp_resume_after_upgrade`), `httpparser.h`'s macros (`llhttp_init`, `llhttp_pause`,
`llhttp_resume`, `llhttp_get_error_reason`) and `llhttp.c`'s 23 dispatchers. No C test,
`http.c` or other C file calls another. The exports keep what that C relies on: the error
position inside the run, the reason a `'static` C string, `llhttp_pause` safe from inside
`on_headers_complete`, and no unwind into C. `libgit2.so` keeps their symbols local
(`--exclude-libs`, `utf8.c`'s switch). No offline C test drives the HTTP client:
`tests/libgit2/core/features.c` only names the parser. So after the switch the exports are
checked by the gateway's eight `unit_priv` tests, which then always compile, by the safe API's
`unit_pub` and `ub_safe` tests, and by libgit2's `online` suites (`online::clone`,
`online::fetch`, `online::push` over HTTP), which the C baseline disables and need the network.

The third switch, `deps/llhttp/api.c`'s (`modules/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c/integration/run-1`),
ran items 1 to 4's scripts unchanged and met four more gaps:

10. **The switch's Rust side precedes the generation.** It is the first switch that removes
    raw bindings: 23 functions without an export, with their allowlist entries. Each
    variant's `build` runs `rust-staticlib.sh`, which builds the crate of the checkout with
    `--features bindgen` in campaign mode, checking the committed bindings against the
    variant's headers, and compiles the gateway only once the export feature is gone. So the
    switch's Rust side, the feature deleted, the allowlist pruned and the bindings
    regenerated, comes before `build-variants.sh`, not after the C's removal as the
    procedure's order (the C change, then the variants, then the gates) suggests. The
    bindings are regenerated against the previous generation, whose headers the switch does
    not change.
11. **A module whose exports only an online suite reaches has no C gate.** `c-tests.sh` runs
    the offline suites the baseline records, and no offline C test drives libgit2's HTTP
    client (the module pass's finding): `httpparser.c`, `httpclient.c` and `llhttp.c`'s
    generated parser call the 31 exports only in a fetch, clone or push over HTTP, whose
    suites (`online::*`) the baseline disables, since they need the network. libgit2's own CI
    runs part of them offline, against servers on localhost named by `GITTEST_REMOTE_URL`
    (`ci/test.sh`'s `auth_clone_and_push`, `-sonline::clone::push -sonline::push`).
12. **The equivalence tests that call no C are marked already.** Item 6's step needs each
    retiring test's calls checked. A test that calls C carries `#[cfg_attr(miri, ignore =
    "calls C")]` (the Miri gate's marker), so the tests that lack it are the candidates, a
    mechanical check; here all 21 carry it, and none is carried over.
13. **A CMake file may name the removed source in a property.** `deps/llhttp/CMakeLists.txt`
    globs its sources, as the lesson has it, and also sets
    `set_source_files_properties(api.c http.c llhttp.c PROPERTIES COMPILE_FLAGS …)`. CMake
    ignores a property of a source no target lists, so the file was left unchanged and every
    variant configured and built; the dangling name stays until the last of the three goes.

## Evidence"""
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

lines: archive members of the dev-profile `staticlib`, and does not collect unused sections.
Its exported API does not change.
+The third switch, `deps/llhttp/api.c`'s (`modules/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c/integration/run-1`),
+ran items 1 to 4's scripts unchanged and met four more gaps:
+10. **The switch's Rust side precedes the generation.** It is the first switch that removes
+    raw bindings: 23 functions without an export, with their allowlist entries. Each
+    variant's `build` runs `rust-staticlib.sh`, which builds the crate of the checkout with
+    `--features bindgen` in campaign mode, checking the committed bindings against the
+    variant's headers, and compiles the gateway only once the export feature is gone. So the
+    switch's Rust side, the feature deleted, the allowlist pruned and the bindings
+    regenerated, comes before `build-variants.sh`, not after the C's removal as the
+    procedure's order (the C change, then the variants, then the gates) suggests. The
+    bindings are regenerated against the previous generation, whose headers the switch does
+    not change.
+11. **A module whose exports only an online suite reaches has no C gate.** `c-tests.sh` runs
+    the offline suites the baseline records, and no offline C test drives libgit2's HTTP
+    client (the module pass's finding): `httpparser.c`, `httpclient.c` and `llhttp.c`'s
+    generated parser call the 31 exports only in a fetch, clone or push over HTTP, whose
+    suites (`online::*`) the baseline disables, since they need the network. libgit2's own CI
+    runs part of them offline, against servers on localhost named by `GITTEST_REMOTE_URL`
+    (`ci/test.sh`'s `auth_clone_and_push`, `-sonline::clone::push -sonline::push`).
+12. **The equivalence tests that call no C are marked already.** Item 6's step needs each
+    retiring test's calls checked. A test that calls C carries `#[cfg_attr(miri, ignore =
+    "calls C")]` (the Miri gate's marker), so the tests that lack it are the candidates, a
+    mechanical check; here all 21 carry it, and none is carried over.
+13. **A CMake file may name the removed source in a property.** `deps/llhttp/CMakeLists.txt`
+    globs its sources, as the lesson has it, and also sets
+    `set_source_files_properties(api.c http.c llhttp.c PROPERTIES COMPILE_FLAGS …)`. CMake
+    ignores a property of a source no target lists, so the file was left unchanged and every
+    variant configured and built; the dangling name stays until the last of the three goes.

# The packaging gate's procedure, for a crate whose dependencies are unpublished
Status: `open`.
## Signal
A procedure worked out by hand that a skill should state: `testing-gates`' Regressions
section says that a batch that changes the raw bindings packages the safe crate, "built
alone in bundled mode from the C it packages, with no build variant selected", and that
"each crate the package depends on is patched to its local source", but not how. The
direct form fails, and the steps that pass were found by trial.
## Evidence
`wave-229/batch-0/run-1` (`src/util/utf8.c`, which allowlists three functions), on base
`2216b0cd0`, the first packaging gate since the tree's change of 2026-11-13:
1. `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT= cargo package --offline --allow-dirty` stops before verifying:
   `no matching package named glibc-bindings found` (crates.io index). The packaged
   manifest drops the Git source of `glibc-bindings` and the path of `ffibox`, keeping
   their versions, and the workspace's `[patch]` tables, keyed by those sources, do not
   apply to it.
2. `cargo package --offline --allow-dirty --no-verify --exclude-lockfile` packages (697
   files). Extracted under `crustify/tmp/`, the package's manifest needs an empty
   `[workspace]`, since the worktree's own encloses it, and
   `[patch.crates-io] glibc-bindings = { path = "/target/glibc-crustify" }` and
   `ffibox = { path = "/crustify-rs/ffibox" }`.
3. `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT= cargo build --offline` there then fails in CMake: PCRE2, then
   zlib, not found. The host has neither: the bundled build finds them only through the
   side campaigns' `plain` installs, `OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR` and `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`, the
   latter `:`-separated in the environment where `build.json`'s `-D` form takes `;`.
   With `OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR=<openssl install>` and
   `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=<openssl install>:<pcre2 install>:<zlib install>`, the package
   builds alone: cmake builds `libgit2.a` and `libcrustify_git2.a` into `OUT_DIR`.
`modules/git2/src/cli/opt.c/integration/run-1` (the switch of `src/cli/opt.c`, on
`f68ea8660`), the next packaging gate, followed steps 2 and 3 and failed to compile the
package's `lib`: two copies of ffibox, `0.1.1` by path for the crate and `0.1.0` by Git
(`40621a2`) for `glibc-bindings`, whose manifest takes ffibox by Git. The workspace patches
that Git source too (`[patch."https://github.com/crustify-rs/ffibox"]`), and step 2's
`[patch.crates-io]` does not stand for it. `opt.rs`'s gateway, which compiles from this switch
on, is the first code of the crate to pass a `glibc_bindings` `FileRef` through the crate's
own ffibox traits (`FileRef::from_ptr`, E0599 four times), so `utf8.c`'s gate could not have
met it. With the workspace's Git patch copied into the package's manifest as well, and the
lockfile the first attempt wrote removed, so that the patch applies, the graph holds one
ffibox and the package builds alone (696 files). Its `lib` tests: 829 pass and 58 fail, the
58 needing `c/tests/resources`, as at `utf8.c`'s gate. So the script copies every `[patch]`
table of the workspace, the Git sources' as well as crates.io's, and resolves with no
lockfile.
## Destination
The spec: `testing-gates`' Regressions section, with a script beside it, as `authoring`
places a procedure that must run exactly so, documented by its `--help`: it packages
without verifying, patches each unpublished dependency to the source the workspace's
`[patch]` names for it, gives the extracted package a workspace of its own, puts the
out-of-tree libraries' installs of the `plain` variant on the build system's search paths,
and builds it with no variant, in a scratch dir it removes.
## Change
Not made: the gate is not a translator's to change. The section would name the script,
and say that the patches and search paths stand in for what a dependent's host supplies.
## Validation
The run above, step by step: step 1 fails as quoted, steps 2 and 3 pass. A script is
validated by passing on that tree and failing, naming the library, without the search
paths.

Where `deps/llhttp/api.c`'s switch went (its commits on the module's branch, the fork's
`c54c0c180`, and its dashboard Notes entry, `libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c` integration):

- Items 1 to 4: `build-variants.sh` built `crustify/builds.gen3` from `c54c0c180`, five
  variants in about 20 minutes at 12 jobs each (item 8's split again, for the 64 the run was
  capped at), each archive holding 210 objects where gen2's held 211, `api.c.o` gone. In
  every variant, `libgit2.so`, `git2` and `libgit2_tests` define the 31 exports (`addr2line`
  puts `llhttp_execute` at `api.rs:1634`) and none of api.c's 23 unexported functions; each
  passed its smoke test (`util_tests -sutf8`). `libgit2.so` defines the same 907 dynamic
  symbols as gen2's, and holds 6747 local Rust functions where gen2's held 6337 (item 9).
  `c-tests.sh` ran unchanged.
- Item 10: the run deleted the feature, pruned `sys/libgit2/allowlist.txt` of the 23
  functions and regenerated `bindings.rs` (`CRUSTIFY_BINDINGS_UPDATE=1 cargo-variant.sh plain
  build --features bindgen --lib`, against gen2), committed that, and only then committed the
  C change and ran `build-variants.sh`, whose `rust-staticlib.sh` then checked the committed
  bindings against gen3's headers on every variant.
- Item 11: the run added `crustify/scripts/http-remote.py`, `git http-backend` behind a
  persistent HTTP/1.1 front that frames each response by its path (`Content-Length`,
  chunked in 1, 7, 4096 and 65536-byte chunks, chunked with chunk extensions, or
  close-delimited), with an optional Basic challenge, and `crustify/scripts/http-gate.sh`,
  which runs a variant's `git2 clone` of two repositories through each framing, three
  clones that fail, and `libgit2_tests -sonline::push -sonline::clone::credentials` with
  `GITTEST_REMOTE_URL` at the guarded remote, into a `results.txt` free of times, ports and
  paths. Gen2's and gen3's results are compared with `diff` (the dashboard entry).
- Item 12: `grep -c 'ignore = "calls C"'` over `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/api.rs` gives 21,
  its `#[test]` count; the module pass's map (`wave-194/batch-7`'s `misc` report) names the
  unit tests that keep each.
- Item 13: `deps/llhttp/CMakeLists.txt` unchanged; gen3's five `configure`s and builds
  passed with it.
- Item 7 again: `wave-194/batch-7/equiv/execute-export-moves-an-empty-runs-error-pos`'s
  reproducer names `ffi-export-deps-llhttp-api-c`, and is left reproducing at the commit its
  report names.

## Destination"""
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
old="""- `bindgen`, Build modes, or the fork's `SelectRust.cmake` (item 9): the C library's link
  collects the Rust it does not call.
"""
new=old+"""- `porting-workflow`, Builds (item 10): the switch's Rust side, the bindings regenerated,
  lands before the generation is built, since every variant's build checks them.
- `testing-gates`, Regressions (item 11): a switch whose exports only the baseline's disabled
  online suites reach runs those the target's own CI runs against local servers, against a
  local remote, by the scripts beside `c-tests.sh`, on the new generation and the previous
  one, compared; `http-remote.py` and `http-gate.sh` generalized from libgit2's suites and
  variables into arguments.
- `porting-workflow`, One language per module (item 12): the carry-over candidates are the
  retiring tests without the Miri `calls C` marker.
- The `libgit2` CMake lesson (item 13): a property naming the removed file is left.
"""
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

entry='''### `libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c` integration: the switch from C

The campaign's third switch, run by `modules/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c/integration/run-1` on the
module's branch, after the merge of the working branch (`a4335ab7a`): `21c5c5f47`, and the fork's
`c54c0c180`. It followed the procedure of `utf8.c`'s and `opt.c`'s switches
(`crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure`) with their scripts unchanged. The export feature
`ffi-export-deps-llhttp-api-c` is deleted, so `api.rs`'s gateway compiles from now on, and its
eight `unit_priv` tests run in `lib`. No export feature is left. The remaining C calls the 31
exports: `transports/httpparser.c` calls `llhttp_execute`, `llhttp_finish`,
`llhttp_get_error_pos` and `llhttp_resume_after_upgrade`, `httpparser.h`'s macros, which
`httpclient.c` expands, call `llhttp_init`, `llhttp_pause`, `llhttp_resume` and
`llhttp_get_error_reason`, and `llhttp.c`'s generated parser calls the 23 `llhttp__on_*`
dispatchers. The raw bindings of the eight functions stay and reach the exports. The dispatchers
have no header declaration and no raw binding. The 23 functions bound without an export go with
their allowlist entries: the seven getters, the three name functions, `llhttp_settings_init`,
`llhttp_reset`, `llhttp_set_error_reason` and the ten lenient setters. Only api.c's equivalence
tests called them, and `bindings.rs` was regenerated without them. Removing them changes the
crate's raw API, `sys::libgit2`, as the porting workflow's switch has it; the safe API does not
change. The types stay for the layouts `httpparser.c` and `llhttp.c` build and read.
`deps/llhttp/api.c` leaves `c/` on the local `fork/main` as `integrate deps/llhttp/api.c`,
which is not pushed. `llhttp.h` stays for `llhttp.c`, `http.c` and the HTTP client.
`deps/llhttp/CMakeLists.txt` globs its sources and is unchanged; its
`set_source_files_properties(api.c http.c llhttp.c …)` names the removed file, and CMake ignores
it. The module has no tied C test. The doc comment that counted nine functions C calls now says
eight.

The module's 21 `equiv` tests are retired with the C they compared (`tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/api.rs`
and its `mod api;`). Each calls C, api.c's own or `llhttp.c`'s parse through it, and carries the
Miri `calls C` marker, so none is carried over. The module pass (`wave-194/batch-7`'s `misc`
report) maps each to the unit tests that keep its behaviour. What none keeps is the
differential itself. The parser's private state was compared byte for byte with C's from six
states, and the lenient setters were shown to read any nonzero `int` as true. Once the C is gone,
nothing is left to compare with. `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs` stays: it compares
`llhttp.c`'s port with its C, whose parse now runs over the Rust dispatchers.

The Rust side landed before the variants were built: every variant's build runs
`rust-staticlib.sh`, which checks the committed bindings and compiles the gateway (proposal's
item 10). The variants were rebuilt as `crustify/builds.gen3` from `c54c0c180` with
`build-variants.sh`, at 12 jobs each so that the five stayed within the host's 64. This
worktree's `crustify/builds` links to gen3, and gen2 was left untouched. Each archive holds 210
objects where gen2's held 211, `api.c.o` gone. In every variant, `libgit2.so`, `git2` and
`libgit2_tests` define the 31 exports and none of api.c's 23 other functions. `addr2line` puts
`llhttp_execute` at `api.rs:1634`. Each variant passed its smoke test (`util_tests -sutf8`,
`git2 --version`). `libgit2.so`'s dynamic symbol table defines the same 907 symbols. It now
holds 6747 local Rust functions where gen2's held 6337 (proposal's item 9).

Gates, over gen3 from `end-gates` snapshots at 64 jobs. The workspace is formatted, and `clippy
--workspace --all-targets` passes with warnings denied. Plain passes the whole workspace:
`lib` 901 and 1 ignored, `equiv` 532, `ub_safe` 796, `ub_unsafe` 144, `unit_pub` 218,
`hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 101 and 397. ASan+UBSan and TSan pass it but for the known nightly
failures: the 9 `compile_fail` snapshots, the six `checkout_*`,
`diff_parse_options_no_raw_conversion`, `odb_options_no_raw_conversion` and
`progress_callback_not_send`, and the `CommitBuilder` doctest (E0624). Neither printed a
sanitizer report. The gateway's eight tests pass on plain, ASan+UBSan and TSan, the first time
under TSan. Miri passes every binary: `lib` 441, `ub_safe` 212, `unit_pub` 141, `equiv` 38,
`ub_unsafe` 26, the rest marked. The gateway's tests are among them: six pass, and
`llhttp_init_initialises_storage_and_stores_what_c_passes` and
`llhttp_execute_keeps_an_empty_runs_error_pos_at_data` are marked `calls C`. The remaining C
tests ran over the link with the Rust through `c-tests.sh`. Plain, ASan+UBSan and TSan give 3443
passed and 55 skipped of 3498, coverage 3444 and 54, each the baseline's record. Under TSan, the
same 10 suites as the baseline's report the C's lock-order inversions and races, and no case
fails; no report has a Rust frame. `ctest` passes both targets on plain, ASan+UBSan and
coverage. Under TSan it fails `offline` on those reports alone, 49 lock-order inversions and
glibc's `tzset` race, as at the two switches before. BSan was rebuilt and not run, as the
settings' `sanitizers` answer has it.

No offline C test drives the HTTP client, and the baseline disables the online suites. So this
switch checked the exports through libgit2's own C over a smart-HTTP remote on localhost:
`crustify/scripts/http-remote.py`, `git http-backend` behind an HTTP/1.1 front with persistent
connections, and `crustify/scripts/http-gate.sh` (proposal's item 11). The front frames each
response by its path: `Content-Length`, chunked in 1, 7, 4096 and 65536-byte chunks, chunked
with chunk extensions, close-delimited, or a header block llhttp refuses. One remote asks for
Basic credentials. The variant's `git2` cloned `testrepo.git` and a three-commit repository of
the source revision's tree through the first three framings, each clone's refs, HEAD, checkout
and `fsck --connectivity-only` checked. It also ran four clones that fail: close-delimited ("could
not read refs from remote repository"), malformed ("http parser error: Invalid header token",
the reason read through `llhttp_get_error_reason`), 404 and 401. Through each of the first three
framings, `libgit2_tests -sonline::push -sonline::clone::credentials` ran against the guarded
remote with `GITTEST_REMOTE_URL`, as libgit2's CI runs `auth_clone_and_push`, and passed 23 with
1 skipped. Gen2's C and gen3's Rust give the same `results.txt` on plain, ASan+UBSan and TSan, and
gen3's coverage variant gives it too: every outcome, every clone's refs, and the requests each
remote answered, by method, framing and status. No run printed a sanitizer report. On the
coverage variant, the run called 24 of the 31 exports, the chunk-extension dispatchers
included, and covered `api.rs`'s 128 of 175 lines and 31 of 44 functions. The seven it never
calls are `on_url` and `on_method` and their `_complete`s, which only a request parse calls,
`on_reset` and `llhttp_resume_after_upgrade`, which need pipelined or upgraded messages, and
`llhttp_finish`, which libgit2 calls only when the socket ends inside a body. The gateway's
`unit_priv` tests cover all seven. The results are kept in the run dir
(`http-gate-results.txt`), for the switches of `http.c` and `llhttp.c` to compare with.

`c/` changed, so the crate was packaged as `package-gate-procedure` has it, with the workspace's
Git patch of ffibox, as at `opt.c`'s switch. It has 695 files, `api.c` out, and builds alone in
bundled mode, where `llhttp.c`'s dispatchers resolve to the Rust. Its `lib` tests: 843 pass, the
gateway's eight among them. The other 58 need the fixture repositories of `c/tests/resources`,
as at the two switches before.

From the switch on, the module's coverage is its Rust's, and the C figures lose `api.c`'s 283
lines. This run did not measure the workspace's coverage. What this switch shows the procedure
lacks is added to `crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure` (items 10 to 13). The review
reproducer that enables the deleted feature (`wave-194/batch-7/equiv/execute-export-moves-an-empty-runs-error-pos`)
is left as it is, reproducing at the commit its report names. Usage cells are the assistant's.

'''

EOF

+`rust-staticlib.sh`, which checks the committed bindings and compiles the gateway (proposal's
+item 10). The variants were rebuilt as `crustify/builds.gen3` from `c54c0c180` with
+`build-variants.sh`, at 12 jobs each so that the five stayed within the host's 64. This
+worktree's `crustify/builds` links to gen3, and gen2 was left untouched. Each archive holds 210
+objects where gen2's held 211, `api.c.o` gone. In every variant, `libgit2.so`, `git2` and
+`libgit2_tests` define the 31 exports and none of api.c's 23 other functions. `addr2line` puts
+`llhttp_execute` at `api.rs:1634`. Each variant passed its smoke test (`util_tests -sutf8`,
+`git2 --version`). `libgit2.so`'s dynamic symbol table defines the same 907 symbols. It now
+holds 6747 local Rust functions where gen2's held 6337 (proposal's item 9).
+Gates, over gen3 from `end-gates` snapshots at 64 jobs. The workspace is formatted, and `clippy
+--workspace --all-targets` passes with warnings denied. Plain passes the whole workspace:
+`lib` 901 and 1 ignored, `equiv` 532, `ub_safe` 796, `ub_unsafe` 144, `unit_pub` 218,
+`hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 101 and 397. ASan+UBSan and TSan pass it but for the known nightly
+failures: the 9 `compile_fail` snapshots, the six `checkout_*`,
+`diff_parse_options_no_raw_conversion`, `odb_options_no_raw_conversion` and
+`progress_callback_not_send`, and the `CommitBuilder` doctest (E0624). Neither printed a
+sanitizer report. The gateway's eight tests pass on plain, ASan+UBSan and TSan, the first time
+under TSan. Miri passes every binary: `lib` 441, `ub_safe` 212, `unit_pub` 141, `equiv` 38,
+`ub_unsafe` 26, the rest marked. The gateway's tests are among them: six pass, and
+`llhttp_init_initialises_storage_and_stores_what_c_passes` and
+`llhttp_execute_keeps_an_empty_runs_error_pos_at_data` are marked `calls C`. The remaining C
+tests ran over the link with the Rust through `c-tests.sh`. Plain, ASan+UBSan and TSan give 3443
+passed and 55 skipped of 3498, coverage 3444 and 54, each the baseline's record. Under TSan, the
+same 10 suites as the baseline's report the C's lock-order inversions and races, and no case
+fails; no report has a Rust frame. `ctest` passes both targets on plain, ASan+UBSan and
+coverage. Under TSan it fails `offline` on those reports alone, 49 lock-order inversions and
+glibc's `tzset` race, as at the two switches before. BSan was rebuilt and not run, as the
+settings' `sanitizers` answer has it.
+No offline C test drives the HTTP client, and the baseline disables the online suites. So this
+switch checked the exports through libgit2's own C over a smart-HTTP remote on localhost:
+`crustify/scripts/http-remote.py`, `git http-backend` behind an HTTP/1.1 front with persistent
+connections, and `crustify/scripts/http-gate.sh` (proposal's item 11). The front frames each
+response by its path: `Content-Length`, chunked in 1, 7, 4096 and 65536-byte chunks, chunked
+with chunk extensions, close-delimited, or a header block llhttp refuses. One remote asks for
+Basic credentials. The variant's `git2` cloned `testrepo.git` and a three-commit repository of
+the source revision's tree through the first three framings, each clone's refs, HEAD, checkout
+and `fsck --connectivity-only` checked. It also ran four clones that fail: close-delimited ("could
+not read refs from remote repository"), malformed ("http parser error: Invalid header token",
+the reason read through `llhttp_get_error_reason`), 404 and 401. Through each of the first three
+framings, `libgit2_tests -sonline::push -sonline::clone::credentials` ran against the guarded
+remote with `GITTEST_REMOTE_URL`, as libgit2's CI runs `auth_clone_and_push`, and passed 23 with
+1 skipped. Gen2's C and gen3's Rust give the same `results.txt` on plain, ASan+UBSan and TSan, and
+gen3's coverage variant gives it too: every outcome, every clone's refs, and the requests each
+remote answered, by method, framing and status. No run printed a sanitizer report. On the
+coverage variant, the run called 24 of the 31 exports, the chunk-extension dispatchers
+included, and covered `api.rs`'s 128 of 175 lines and 31 of 44 functions. The seven it never
+calls are `on_url` and `on_method` and their `_complete`s, which only a request parse calls,

+`llhttp_finish`, which libgit2 calls only when the socket ends inside a body. The gateway's

content.text:
`api.c` has switched from C to Rust and every gate passed, with only the known failures. Nothing was pushed and no remote changed.

**Commits**
- `21c5c5f47`, *api.c: switch from C to Rust (modules/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c/integration/run-1)*: the Rust side, plus the superproject's record of the new fork commit.
- `0c1bd7a0d`, the records: the dashboard Notes entry, the run's `task.json`, `task.md` and `http-gate-results.txt`, two new scripts, and the proposal's new evidence.
- Fork: `c54c0c180`, *integrate deps/llhttp/api.c*, on local `fork/main`, which removes `deps/llhttp/api.c` and keeps `llhttp.h`.

**What changed**
- **Export feature:** deleted, so the gateway in `api.rs` and its 8 tests now compile.
- **Equivalence tests:** the 21 tests in `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/api.rs` are retired with their `mod` line. All of them call C and carry the Miri `calls C` marker, so none was carried over.
- **Raw bindings:** the 8 exported functions keep theirs. The 23 functions with no export lost their allowlist entries, and `bindings.rs` was regenerated without them. This changes the crate's raw `sys::libgit2` API; the safe API is unchanged.

**New build generation**
- `crustify/builds.gen3` was built with `build-variants.sh`, at 12 jobs per variant to stay within 64. This worktree's `crustify/builds` now links to it; gen2 is untouched.
- Each archive holds 210 objects instead of 211, with `api.c.o` gone.
- In every variant, `libgit2.so`, `git2` and `libgit2_tests` take the 31 exports from `api.rs`.

**Gates**
- **fmt and clippy:** pass, with warnings denied.
- **Plain:** the whole workspace passes: `lib` 901 (1 ignored), `equiv` 532, `ub_safe` 796, `ub_unsafe` 144, `unit_pub` 218, doctests 101 and 397.
- **ASan/UBSan and TSan:** pass apart from the 9 known `compile_fail` snapshots and the `CommitBuilder` doctest, with no sanitizer report.
- **Miri:** passes every test binary.
- **Remaining C tests (`c-tests.sh`):** plain, ASan/UBSan, TSan and coverage each match `c-baseline.json`. Under TSan, `ctest` fails `offline` only on the C's own lock-order inversions and glibc's `tzset` race, with no Rust frame, as at the two earlier switches.
- **Packaging:** the crate packages (695 files) and builds alone in bundled mode, with ffibox's Git patch. Its `lib` tests: 843 pass; the 58 failures need the fixture repositories the package leaves out.
- **BSan:** rebuilt, not run.

**What exercises the exports through libgit2's own C**
No offline C test reaches libgit2's HTTP client, so I added two scripts under `crustify/scripts/`:
- `http-remote.py` serves repositories over HTTP on localhost through `git http-backend`. It frames responses five ways (Content-Length, chunked, chunked with extensions, close-delimited, malformed), and one instance asks for a password.
- `http-gate.sh` runs the variant's `git2 clone` against it, plus libgit2's own `online::push` and `online::clone::credentials` tests via `GITTEST_REMOTE_URL`.

Gen2's C and gen3's Rust gave identical results on plain, ASan/UBSan and TSan, with no sanitizer report.

On the coverage variant, that run calls 24 of the 31 exports. The other 7 can't be reached from a client:
- the URL and method dispatchers (4) only fire when parsing a request;
- `on_reset` and `llhttp_resume_after_upgrade` need pipelined or upgraded responses;
- `llhttp_finish` runs only at a body's end of file.

The gateway's own tests cover six of those seven. `llhttp_resume_after_upgrade` has no test of its own; only the method it wraps is tested in `unit_pub`. That gap is still open.

**Gates rerun:** there was no rebase or landing. The gates above ran on the switch commit `21c5c5f47`. The records commit changes only docs, scripts and the run dir.

**Procedure evidence** added to `crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure`:
- 10: the Rust side, including the regenerated bindings, must land before the new generation is built, because every variant's build checks the bindings.
- 11: a module whose exports only network tests reach needs a localhost HTTP check. The two scripts for it are made, in the campaign only.
- 12: the Miri `calls C` marker is a mechanical way to find the equivalence tests worth carrying over.
- 13: `deps/llhttp/CMakeLists.txt` still names `api.c` in a property. CMake ignores it, so I left it, as the lesson says.

Also:
- The job count again had to be split by hand across the variants (existing item 8).
- I fixed `api.rs`'s doc comment, which counted nine functions called from C; there are eight.
- The review reproducer that enables the deleted feature is left as it was.

Scratch under `crustify/tmp/` is deleted. Usage cells are yours.
